exempt.PousCheck.SetupProtocolMain: the pous-setup executable's entry point, one line; its command is Core.Protocol.main of PousCheck.SetupProtocol.protocol, audited under PousCheck and CoreProtocol
exempt.PousCheck.SetupDifftestMain: the pous-setup-difftest server's entry point, one line: Difftest.serve of PousCheck.SetupDifftest.table, which tests/test_setup_difftest.py drives against the Python reference; audited under PousCheck
exempt.PousCheck.DifftestMain: the difftest against the Python verifier, under `runs`: compiled evaluation of PousCheck.Difftest.main, audited under PousCheck, a test and not a proof; with `serve`, Difftest.serve of PousCheck.Difftest.transcript, which interop.py drives against wire.py

PousCheck.DifftestMain.why: generated instances on which PousCheck's definitions give what the Python verifier gives: the verification tree (reference.leaf, verifier.leaf_hash, root, path, wire.path_length, verify_path on honest and tampered paths), the challenges (verity.ml.randomness; reference.audit_id, audit_key, round_key, each round's index and nonce), and the timed audit (wire.verify_audit's FINAL frame, fault or refusal on honest and adversarial sessions, at reduced width and at the deployment's, with the verifier's own root of a private setup, a wrong or missing one, a required seen set, flag bit 1 against a held, wrong or missing W, and an elapsed time past u64, and on the spec's 31 negative and 3 positive audit vectors), the certificate gate and StorageProfile (protocol.TimedAudit with P2's deadline refusals, and StorageProfile at schemes.p2.P2) of every accepted session and of 200 stores and audits at the certificate's edges, with the spec's section 7 pins of the audit files and frames

PousCheck.why: the program is code: Lean core, Flock's executable primitives, the core protocol interface and the core primitives (identity, randomness) only, no Mathlib and nothing of Security (Daniel's layout ruling, 5 Oct)
